## TL;DR

If the green-checkpoint (or a pot cup's `test:affected`) goes red on:

```
lib/harness/git-sync/multi-peer-convergence.test.ts
Test: "the losing peer conflicts INSIDE the submodule, does NOT publish a broken
       gitlink, then the fleet converges"
Error: git cat-file -e <hash>^{commit} failed (128):
       fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

**Do not re-diagnose it as a submodule / gitlink / convergence logic bug.** At
least four SU sessions have now traced it (su-1897a, su-aaee9, su-ca91b, and the
session that wrote this page) and reached the same verdict: **the convergence
LOGIC is correct; this is a non-deterministic box-weather flake.** `main`
self-advances past it on the next checkpoint run — confirm with
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <blocker-sha> origin/main` before spending any time
on it (on 2026-06-13 the blocker held main at `6d044f9b`; the next run advanced
it 18 commits to `b55e1a5f4`).

## Why it is NOT a logic bug (the evidence)

The file passes **deterministically** under every condition that isn't extreme
full-suite load:

- `npx vitest run …/multi-peer-convergence.test.ts` in isolation — 6/6 green,
  repeatably (every prior diagnoser confirmed this).
- **12× concurrent** self-execution at box load ~30 — all 12 exit 0, zero git
  errors. (The flake is not simple inter-process `/tmp` contention.)
- Forced **`--testTimeout=1200`** (sub-2s) — still 6/6 green in ~8s, because even
  the heavy submodule test completes in well under a second of wall-clock git
  work on a quiet box.

A genuine convergence/gitlink defect would fail in isolation. This one cannot be
made to fail except under the real full-`test:affected` shard at pathological
load — exactly the "box weather" the unit config's own comment documents
(`libs/test-config/src/vitest-config.ts`: green-checkpoint went red twice "purely
on 20_000ms timeouts … ALL passing in isolation … with the box at load ~135").

## The mechanism (most-consistent hypothesis)

The error text is unambiguously this file's own `git()` helper throwing at the
**last** assertion of the submodule test (`cat-file -e <pointer>^{commit}` in the
submodule's bare origin). The selectivity puzzle — the two `git` calls on the
same bare repo *immediately before* (`rev-parse main`, `ls-tree main`) succeed —
rules out an env leak (`GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`: no operator-core test mutates
them) and rules out a sibling test (this is the only git-sync test with both the
`failed (<code>)` throw-helper format and a `cat-file …^{commit}`). The remaining
mechanism that fits *"passes in isolation + flakes only under load + surfaces as
an unhandled rejection that fails the whole run"*:

1. Under extreme load the heavy real-git test (clones super+sub, N peers,
   `convergeFleet` up to 20 rounds × per-peer `runGitSync` × `resolveScope` up to
   8 push passes — many real `git` subprocesses) overruns the 60s unit timeout.
2. vitest marks the test timed-out and tears the **file** down, but JS cannot
   cancel the in-flight async — the test body keeps running and its
   `finally { await rm(tmpRoot, { recursive, force }) }` deletes the temp tree.
3. A `git` call that is still in flight (or runs just after) now resolves against
   a **deleted** working/temp dir → `git()` throws `not a git repository` in an
   async chain vitest is no longer awaiting → **unhandled rejection** → vitest
   reds the *entire* run, attributing the git error to whatever test is "current."

So the confusing part — a `cat-file` "not a git repository" that looks like a
broken gitlink — is a **teardown artifact**, not a published-pointer defect. The
"published superproject pointer is unreachable on the submodule origin" reading
is a red herring.

(Not fully reproduced: forcing the exact stranded-rejection sequence needs the
real ~135 box load, which a quiet box can't manufacture. The *negative* claim —
"not a convergence logic bug" — is what's proven, and it's the one that matters.)

## What to do

- **Nothing urgent.** It self-clears; `main` advances on the next green run.
  Don't hand it to a merge-resolver, don't edit the convergence assertions, don't
  "fix the gitlink."
- **Do NOT weaken the assertions.** The `maxRounds: 20` / 8-pass resolver bounds
  ARE the no-ping-pong proof (P-004) — shrinking them to dodge the timeout would
  delete the property the test exists to verify.
- A real fix (owner / B-02 lane, `shared-pot-hardening-2026-06-13`) would make
  the heavy real-git tests **not strand an unhandled rejection on teardown** — so
  a load timeout fails cleanly as *itself* instead of reddening the whole run and
  mis-pointing the next investigator at a phantom convergence bug. That needs a
  repro under genuine extreme load, which is why it's gated on the owner's rig,
  not a blind edit.
